pr_title: Disable activation of overlays while in gameplay
pr_body:
Closes #9743
Alternative to / supersedes  #9751

# Summary

This adds the ability to disable activation of overlays while in gameplay through a setting that defaults to true. Overlay activation is re-enabled back if the gameplay is paused, enters a break period or the current gameplay is running a replay.
pr_comments:
I've pushed in a menial change that aims to avoid having `OverlayActivation.UserTriggered` specified in two places (now they both refer to a single constant). Unfortunately this can't be done without introducing the constant.

Otherwise this seems ok. In a quick gameplay test it works roughly as expected - the only issue is that the hotkeys make a click sound even if disabled, but that should probably be fixed globally as I imagine it'll be a global issue and is probably out of scope here.

Not approving since I pushed.

Oh, and also this should allow overlay activation on break times as well, these aren't "gameplay" periods and it's also kind of a normal habit for a player to open the chat overlay and talk there in such periods.
Honestly, with the amount of complexity here, I wonder if this even needs to be a setting? Is there a use case for setting the setting to false?

About the first paragraph in https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/9766#pullrequestreview-463824776, here's what I think of how should `OverlayActivationMode` be mutable (with `OsuGame` itself being responsible for it): https://github.com/frenzibyte/osu/compare/1398234b1bc54fe2e09158ef7aaac929b7209ec8...6285cd4b108985c02461ddf58590745e89d105b7

That would get rid of any unorganized insurances inside `Player` (binding at `OnEntering`, ensuring `OverlayActivationMode` isn't change while not in current screen), would like to hear if it's going the right direction before PRing though.
Changing InitialOverlayActivation to just be a screen bindable and is one-way bound with the game one should work amicably.

> 
> Honestly, with the amount of complexity here, I wonder if this even needs to be a setting? Is there a use case for setting the setting to false?

I'm fine with dropping the setting and having this as a default behaviour, as it would also resolve the issue where the overlay activation mode would change because the setting value was updated despite the player being suspended.

issue_context.title: Add an option to disable "ctr + key actions" in game
issue_context.body:
**Describe the new feature:** 

As a mania player, I use s-d-f-space-j-k-l for playing, and on many occasions, I have pressed without intention the ctrl key with my left hand while playing, opening direct overlay, (ctr + d) and that has led me to lose several times.
I would like to have an option in the menu to disable ctr + key actions (just as the windows key) to disable these actions in gameplay.

**Proposal designs of the feature:** 

As an option in the main menu where you can choose to disable these actions if they bother you as it does for me.
comments: Can you confirm you still want these keys to be on ctrl-<key> when not in gameplay? because a possible solution is to just bind them to something else, if not.

It may be easier to add an option that disables hotkeys that interrupt gameplay (like calling certain overlays) while playing. This would allow to not just intercept ctrl based hotkeys but other types as well (if rebound for example).

> Can you confirm you still want these keys to be on ctrl- when not in gameplay? because a possible solution is to just bind them to something else, if not.

It is a solution but I am used to the ctr + key bindings tbh, I like the solution given above rather than changing key bindings, since for sure it will happen to someone else in the future.

review_comments:
nit: not sure about the wording here, try **pausing** and changing the skin while **playing**, maybe
```csharp
…. Try pausing and changing the skin while in a gameplay.
```
of course, that's what the **maybe** is for, I'm pointing that there's kind of an oxymoron here that shouldn't really exist in such place. (or anywhere)
I don't really think this needed to change.
maybe not... I'm just super not looking forward to potentially having someone claim that the tip is wrong because "settings menu can't be opened during gameplay"
would also like a test case for allowing the overlays to be opened by disabling the setting here for completeness

In fact, I had a test to ensure that overlays can be opened when the setting is disabled, but I ended up not committing it as for some reason the setting update doesn't propagate to the loaded test player (whereas this works just fine in game), making the test always fail.
That is quite unsettling. I'd like to know why exactly it fails in the test.

the test doesn't work because it's using the wrong instance of `OsuConfigManager`. `PlayerTestScene` creates and caches its own:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/c09868780e1d03703a18f37e512777fba3afe89c/osu.Game/Tests/Visual/PlayerTestScene.cs#L25-L32

using that one instead of the locally-`[Resolved]` config manager fixes the failure.

on that note I'd also like to say that I find the mentality of discarding the test if it doesn't work correctly quite dangerous. we shouldn't become accustomed to accepting that things just don't work sometimes for unknown reasons. if I hadn't prodded continuously reviewing this, I probably wouldn't have found out that the tests were half-broken due to using the wrong config instance, especially seeing that they *read* sane.

(also not sure how to feel about having to debug this myself, but, alas.)
I apologize for having left the debugging of this to you. I feel really bad for doing it, especially when the cause is that I didn't paid attention enough to the existing code.
